column1: What's the difference between e.target and e.currentTarget?
column2: e.target = where the event originated. e.currentTarget = the element the listener is bound to. After an async gap currentTarget is null (dispatch finished) — capture it into a const synchronously.

column1: What does the 3rd arg `true` in addEventListener do?
column2: Registers the listener on the CAPTURE phase — fires on the way DOWN (document to target), before any bubble-phase listener. Paired with stopPropagation to intercept an event before another listener sees it.

column1: What is CustomEvent's `detail`?
column2: The one property CustomEvent reserves for your payload; read back as e.detail in the listener. The event is the call, detail is the argument. dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('x',{detail:data})).

column1: Callback vs closure?
column2: Callback = role (a function passed to be called by another). Closure = nature (every JS function closes over its defining scope). Every callback is a closure; it only USES the closure when it reads an outer variable.

column1: How do you restart a CSS animation from JS?
column2: el.classList.remove('x'); void el.offsetWidth; el.classList.add('x'). Reading offsetWidth forces a synchronous reflow so the remove is 'real' before the re-add — otherwise remove+add in one tick collapses to no-change.

column1: const x = someAsyncFn() — what does x hold?
column2: The Promise, NOT the resolved value. `await x` returns the value but does not mutate x. If you use the value in several places, store the resolved value (e.g. via .then(v => cache = v)).

column1: new Option(label, value) vs building an <option> HTML string?
column2: new Option sets text/value as PROPERTIES — no HTML parsing, so a value with < or & can't break markup (injection-safe). An HTML-string <option> is fragile with those chars.

column1: form.action property vs form.getAttribute('action')?
column2: The .action PROPERTY defaults to the page URL when the attribute is absent. getAttribute('action') returns the literal string or null. Use getAttribute when 'null' should mean 'skip this form'.

column1: Why does a phone field look wrong after form.reset() with inputmask?
column2: reset() clears the value but leaves inputmask's internal buffer stale. Re-apply: $(el).inputmask('remove'); $(el).inputmask(mask).

column1: Rule for a conditional block inside a template literal?
column2: Emit WHOLE elements per branch. Opening a tag in the branch and closing it outside gives a box that works when the condition is true and is broken when false.

column1: When can http_response_code() still change the HTTP status?
column2: Only before the first body byte is sent. Once any echo flushes output, headers+status are locked. Fix: build-then-echo-once, or ob_start() to buffer output.

column1: ob_start / ob_get_clean / ob_clean / ob_end_flush?
column2: ob_start: capture output to a buffer. ob_get_clean: return+discard buffer as a string. ob_clean: discard buffer, keep capturing. ob_end_flush: stop+send buffer. Buffering keeps headers changeable until flush.

column1: var_dump vs ob_* — how do they relate?
column2: var_dump PRODUCES output (a debug lens). ob_* CONTROLS where any output goes (a pipe). Capture a dump as a string: ob_start(); var_dump($x); $s = ob_get_clean();

column1: What does mail() returning true actually mean?
column2: Handed to the local MTA without immediate error — NOT delivered. true = handoff, not delivery. Keep success:true even if mail fails; surface a soft mailQueued:false flag.

column1: require vs require_once?
column2: require_once skips if the file was already included (use for class files to avoid 'Cannot redeclare class'). require always includes.

column1: PHP string interpolation rules?
column2: Double quotes and heredoc interpolate; single quotes are literal. Braces {$expr} are required for array access, method calls, and properties: "{$_POST['x']}".

column1: PHP vs JS interpolation — when does each run?
column2: PHP: server-side, once, as the string is built (browser only sees flat text). JS template literal: client-side, each time the line executes. Same concept, two machines, two moments.

column1: Why replace isAjaxRequest() (X-Requested-With) with a POST check?
column2: jQuery sets X-Requested-With automatically; fetch/axios do not — so the guard is coupled to a JS library. isPostRequest = REQUEST_METHOD==='POST' && !empty($_POST) is library-agnostic.

column1: 405 vs 403 for a refused request?
column2: 403 Forbidden = 'not allowed to'. 405 Method Not Allowed = 'wrong HTTP method' (e.g. a GET where POST is required). The status should name the actual reason.

column1: SQL: find items in list A that have no match in list B?
column2: LEFT JOIN B ON key WHERE b.key IS NULL — the join leaves unmatched A rows with NULL on the B side; filter for those. The standard list-diff pattern.

column1: How to check every POSTed key is a real table column?
column2: SELECT k.name FROM (posted keys as UNION) k LEFT JOIN INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS c ON c.COLUMN_NAME=k.name AND schema/table WHERE c.COLUMN_NAME IS NULL — prints keys with no column (future 1054s).

column1: mysql -e and \\G?
column2: -e "SQL" runs one statement non-interactively, TSV output. End a statement with \\G instead of ; for vertical (one field per line) output.

column1: MySQL strict-mode error fingerprints?
column2: 1054/42S22 = unknown column (schema drift). 1364 = required field with no default (strict only). 1406/22001 = value too long (strict only). 1045 = bad creds. 2002 = host/network.

column1: What does Table::addRow($_POST) do with POST keys?
column2: Inserts EVERY POST key as a column. Any form input that isn't a real column (region toggles, alt-address fields) must be stripped in buildBody or you get 1054 Unknown column.

column1: Open a new line below/above from INSERT mode (built-in)?
column2: <C-o>o opens below, <C-o>O opens above. <C-o> runs one normal-mode command then returns to insert; o/O themselves enter insert on the new line.

column1: How to find where a Neovim mapping was defined?
column2: :verbose imap <key> (or nmap/vmap) — the 'Last set from ...' line names the file/plugin.

column1: Rule of three (refactoring)?
column2: Extract a shared abstraction after the THIRD duplicate, not the second. Two isn't enough to trust the shape. Premature abstraction is worse than duplication.

column1: How to externalize per-case variation cleanly?
column2: As DATA (a registry/config object) or small CALLBACKS (toOption, sort, buildBody) — not copied code. Keep the shell, sanitize, and markup single-source.

column1: Where does payload-shaping (buildBody) end and page UI begin?
column2: buildBody only reshapes/whitelists/validates the payload. UI state (show/hide, region logic) stays on the page. They share no variables — they communicate via the DOM + CustomEvent(detail).

column1: What should a catch block cover?
column2: Only the failure it names. Wrap risky display/render work in its OWN try so a render bug can't fire the 'network error' toast. A catch that straddles two failures will mislabel one.
